source_pr_title: fix(ci): append-only harvest files land on main via bot PR
author: amazon-q-developer
body:
:stop_sign: **Logic Error**: The conditional check for `list_only` is incorrect when event is `pull_request`. When a PR is merged, the workflow should always create a bot PR if there are harvest files, regardless of the `list_only` value which is only applicable to `workflow_dispatch` events. The current condition `github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.inputs.list_only != true` will evaluate `github.event.inputs.list_only` even when it's undefined during PR merge events, which could cause unexpected behavior or workflow failures.
```suggestion
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.list_only != 'true')
```

author: amazon-q-developer
body:
:stop_sign: **Logic Error**: Boolean comparison in GitHub Actions workflow expressions should use string comparison. The `github.event.inputs.list_only` is a string type (`'true'` or `'false'`), not a boolean. Comparing with boolean `true` instead of string `'true'` may cause incorrect evaluation. When `list_only` input is the string `'true'`, the expression `github.event.inputs.list_only != true` will incorrectly evaluate to `true` (string `'true'` != boolean `true`), causing the PR creation step to run even when it should be skipped.
```suggestion
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.inputs.list_only != 'true'
```

source_pr_title: fix(ci): append-only harvest files land on main via bot PR
author: greptile-apps
body: **`debt-summary.json` no longer committed to git** The old step used `git add .agents/review-debt/` (which included `debt-summary.json`); the new step uses `git add .agents/review-debt/harvests/` and omits the summary. `writeSummary` is still called and writes the file to disk inside the runner, but it is never committed. The `debt-summary.json` on `main` will therefore remain frozen at the last pre-migration snapshot, making the hotspot data stale after every harvest bot-PR merge. If the summary is intentionally a derived artifact (not committed), this is fine — but worth explicitly calling out. If it should be kept current in the repo, add it to the staged set alongside the harvest files.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Make bot branch naming rerun-safe to avoid push/PR creation failures.**

Line 117 uses only `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; reruns of the same workflow reuse that id, so `git push`/`gh pr create` can fail against an existing branch and block publication.

   

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-          BRANCH="review-debt/harvest-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
+          BRANCH="review-debt/harvest-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}"
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
          BRANCH="review-debt/harvest-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}"
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]`@users.noreply.github.com`"
          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          git add .agents/review-debt/harvests/

          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            TITLE="chore(review-debt): harvest PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
            BODY="Append-only harvest files under .agents/review-debt/harvests/ (timestamp-pr-run). Merge to add to main without ledger conflicts."
          else
            TITLE="chore(review-debt): harvest batch (run ${{ github.run_id }})"
            BODY="Append-only harvest files from workflow_dispatch run ${{ github.run_id }}. Merge to add to main."
          fi

          git commit -m "$TITLE"
          git push -u origin "$BRANCH"
          gh pr create --base main --head "$BRANCH" --title "$TITLE" --body "$BODY"
```

</details>

suffix (e.g. include GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT or $(date +%s) or $RANDOM) so it's
unique per run (e.g.
BRANCH="review-debt/harvest-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}"); keep the
